title: EEVblog #873 - World's Most Dangerous Consumer Product!
description: Dave looks at possibly the world's most dangerous consumer product, a portable electrode boiler based water heater available on ebay. Marketed as "safe", it is nothing less than a death trap!  EDIT: Holy crap! They sell this as a baby bath heater! http://www.ebay.com/itm/AC-220v-2500w-Bathtub-Baby-Swimming-Pool-Water-Quick-Heater-Heating-Tube-/331669347074?hash=item4d39089b02:g:TaYAAOSw9r1WDGQx  Forum: http://www.eevblog.com/forum/blog/eevblog-873-world's-most-dangerous-consumer-product!/  EEVblog Main Web Site: http://www.eevblog.com The 2nd EEVblog Channel: http://www.youtube.com/EEVblog2  Support the EEVblog through Patreon! http://www.patreon.com/eevblog  EEVblog Amazon Store (Dave gets a cut): http://astore.amazon.com/eevblogstore-20  T-Shirts: http://teespring.com/stores/eevblog :growing heart: Likecoin – Coins for Likes: https://likecoin.pro/@eevblog/dil9/hcq3

asr.full_text: Hi. Check this out. I think I found the world's most dangerous consumer product. Ta-da! Somebody sent this into my mailbag segment. Yes, it's a mains cord connected into some sort of probe thing. Hmm, thank you very much to the person who sent this one in. Uh, no, it's not one of these USB hole warmers that we've seen before on the mailbag, where you plug them in the USB port and stick them up a hole and it warms things up. I'm sure they're just fine. No, it's this thing. It's a portable immersion electric element for heating up water. I'm going to show you why this is the most dangerous consumer product possible. Let's go. So this is a portable immersion jug element you can't get this in the city so I hope I can do it But it's a great tool to work with So we're gonna run this one together Here I'll take a quick look, try not to get myself in trouble I'll try to record myself and show you how it works So now let's play with something really cool This is the new version of an internet service A very small project Not very simple or something like that. And you can probably see, down in there, look! There's metal plates! There's metal plates down in there! Ahh! Connected directly up to a mains cord! Let's measure it. Now according to the eBay page, this is a 500 Watt electric immersion heater, so it should have an element in there. What? No, it doesn't. It doesn't measure anything at all, but what it does do, let's stick one probe on there, one probe on there... Look, it's connected directly to the mains pin, and the other one is connected directly to the other plate! That's all it is! Is the mains cord connected directly to two internal plates it's an electrolysis device for heating water, you gotta be kidding me and here's the actual card it comes with we look just stick it into a jug there no worries whatsoever and its all in chinese for those who can read Chinese but I've actually translated the one in red here and we can see this. This product is available in pots, buckets, cups, beakers, submerge, and portions. Generates power dissipation, not submerge part, does not produce power consumption, i.e. no heat. D.U.E.R., you take it out, it's just two plates, it doesn't heat anything. The actual power consumption and water hardness. The product relies on water and ionic conductivity, so the actual power consumption is a higher than the actual power consumption and water hardness, the product relies on water and ionic conductivity. So the actual power consumption is rated to basically... how... They're saying hardness, but that means how basically contaminated or how not pure the water is. So if you've got really 100% pure water, this thing's not gonna work too well. It's an electrolysis device. You put enough voltage and current, thank you, so if you've got really 100% pure water this thing's not going to work too well. It's an electrolysis device, you put enough voltage and current through water like this and you're going to separate the hydrogen and you're gonna boil the water. Yeah, it's gonna work, it's basic electrolysis but it's the just the most dangerous way to boil water possible. And we got some warnings down here, the... product do not let children near the power cord is damaged or broken protective case. They're concerned about a damaged power cord. Think I'm big concerned about something else and children with this thing. Oh, goodness. So you know all those, um, warning videos About not dropping your hair dryer in the bath and things like that Because, uh, they're connected up to a mains cord If you put them in water and you touch the water YOU CAN DIE OHHH I can't help laughing but this is deadly serious They're selling a product, consumer product, with exposed mains wires that you deliberately stick into water, and look, it's safe, safe. Yeah, look, this couple looks happy here. They're taking their portable electric immersion element with them while they're going camping, and they're just going to stick it in there and warm up their water! Unbelievable but look at the description. This is funny. Microwaves, special materials, non-toxic, odolous in 100 degree water, does not decompose, not aching, not discolouration deformation Due to the magnetic wave action during the heating. After water absorb electromagnetic energy moisture occurs beside the water of not aching, not discolouration, deformation! Due to the magnetic wave-action during the heating , after water absorb electro magnetic energy, moisture occurs, bizarre oscillation, collision, an after friction, the water rise in temperature. But, look at this one. Through special panels, put chlorine, converting into hypochlorite play a roll in disinfection and sterilisation. I'm not very good at chemistry but doesn't heating up chlorine actually, maybe, potentially convert it into a gas, chlorine gas, which is kinda sorta- dangerous? But I know what you're saying. Dave, don't be too harsh on this. Look, after all they have a warning here, and it's in red. It even got a double N, just in case. Don't use metallic or plastic container. Don't heat when the container has no water or enough water. Don't put the device in completely!! When you finish heating, of water or enough water. Don't put the device in water completely! Exclamation marks everywhere! When you finish heating switch off device first, wait 30 seconds and then take the device out. Never touch the element when it is hot! Never put your hands into the water when it is heating. No shit SHERLOCK! Unfortunately, there's 28 people out there who bought just this one from this one seller in this one auction that's it and they have another 100 available ready to ship direct from Hong Kong for $3.89 including postage!! Beauty! And well I don't really have to insult anyone's intelligence by telling you how dangerous it is sticking exposed mains wires directly into water. Like... my five year old would know this. Unbelievable. But people, you know, they see the word safe up here, no worries, like it's plastic, it looks insulated and things like that... so, your average Joe might buy this thinking like, ya know... look says it is safe and has no worries... ...right?! ...you just put in mains wires directly into water, like... POOFF!! so, I shouldn't have to tell not to buy this heap of crap. KILL YOU! OK, don't try this at home. It's alive! It works! Wow, 1 kilowatt! Look at it! There it is! If you're curious about the power factor there we go, it is bang on so no worries so much for the 500 watts... WOW! 1.1 kilowatts! Ah that's ridiculous. And the steam's coming up, or is that hydrogen? Yeah that looks completely safe doesn't it. Awww, that's ridiculous. And the steam's coming up! Or is that hydrogen? Yeah, that looks completely safe, doesn't it? 240 volt mains, two plates straight in the tap water. 1.2 kilowatts now. Unbelievable. Just...no! Hang on... No no no no no no no. No! No! No. No. No! That's right, the damn thing blew up in my hand when I was trying to measure 240 volt mains. I was holding it like this, probing the 240 volts as I do. BANG!!! The damn thing! It didn't literally blow apart, but it was one hell of a Bang and I jumped ten feet across the room, the damn thing near killed me. So clearly there goes the review coz all I've got is a charred meter I don't ever another one to do a review not that I would anyway, coz this thing has a serious safety issue which needs to be addressed. And I think I know, possibly, why it blew up. So let's take a look at it.
